We need to interpret the problem: We can increase/decrease any elements up to k total operations (sum of absolute changes). We want to minimize the score defined as the frequency of the least frequent element in the final array.

Observation: We can change values arbitrarily (including making them equal to other values) but limited by total cost k (the sum of absolute changes across all indices). The score is frequency of the least frequent element; we want it as small as possible. Ideally we'd like to make the least frequent element appear only once (score 1) or maybe even zero? Since we can't have zero frequency of any element because each element present contributes at least one count; we can't eliminate an element entirely unless we change all its occurrences to something else (i.e., we could delete a value by moving all its occurrences to other values). If we can change all occurrences of some value to other values (by paying cost), then that value disappears, and then the least frequent element among remaining values could have higher frequency? Actually we want to minimize the frequency of the least frequent element. If we can make some value appear only once, that yields score 1. If we can make all elements equal, then frequency of least frequent = n (since only one distinct value, frequency = n). That would maximize score, not minimize. Wait: Let's check the definition again: "score of the final array is the frequency of the least frequent element in the array." The least frequent element is the element that appears the fewest times. If we have multiple distinct values, the least frequent could be 1 if any value appears once. If all values appear at least 2 times, the least frequent could be >=2. So to minimize the score we want to make the least frequent as small as possible, ideally 1 (if we can have any element appearing exactly once) or maybe 0? But frequency 0 would mean that element does not appear in the array; but then it's not an element of the array, so we don't consider it. The least frequent element among those present cannot have frequency zero. So minimum possible score is 1 (unless array length is zero, but n>=1). Could we achieve score 0? No.

Thus answer is either 1 (if we can make some element appear exactly once within k operations) or maybe higher if not possible.
